subject.title: iOS app: node requests re-approval on every reconnect (token persistence bug)

question: Should this issue remain open for current-main live iOS reconnect proof before deciding whether volatile iOS permission/watch state needs a code change?
rationale: Source inspection proves an overlapping QR token fix and a plausible remaining reapproval trigger, but only a real current-main iPhone reconnect run can show whether the reported manual-setup loop is still present.

options.title: Run live iOS reconnect proof
options.body: Keep this issue open and verify current-main iOS over the reported LAN/VPN flow before choosing the code shape.

options.title: Close as covered by the QR fix
options.body: Close only if a maintainer already has real-device evidence that the repeated reapproval loop no longer happens after the LAN bootstrap fix.

options.title: Queue a scoped fix after repro
options.body: If live proof confirms volatile permission or capability drift, fix that specific declaration or gateway comparison path with focused native and gateway tests.

recommendation.title: Run live iOS reconnect proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and verify current-main iOS over the reported LAN/VPN flow before choosing the code shape.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged mobile metadata refresh fix is the closest prior maintainer-visible work on mobile reconnect approval churn.
